reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is to present a Chipotle buy-one-get-one food promotion and explain how viewers can obtain the associated coupon. The request to click a description link and provide a name and cell phone number is presented as part of coupon delivery for an ordinary purchase-based offer, rather than as an investment, payment, credential, or other deceptive scheme. The external destination's affiliation and use of the requested information are left uncertified.

citations.quote: They are offering a free burrito when you buy one, a free burrito bowl when you buy one, a free salad when you buy one, or a free order of tacos when you buy one.
All you have to do to get the coupon is click on the link in my description and make your mix of the ingredients you like on your food.
After that, they'll ask you for your name and your cell phone number and then they will text you the coupon!
Now the coupon is good through August 31st but there's a limit of one per person per cell phone number.

opening.argument: The promised free food is conditional on a viewer completing a multi-step claim process, so this is more than a passive promotion. The video directs viewers to click a description link, customize a food order, provide a name and cell phone number, and wait for a coupon by text. The reward is therefore tied directly to an external action and the submission of contact information. Even the offer is framed as “free” only after buying another item, making the advertised benefit dependent on both a purchase and the off-platform claim flow.

citations.quote: They are offering a free burrito when you buy one, a free burrito bowl when you buy one, a free salad when you buy one, or a free order of tacos when you buy one.
All you have to do to get the coupon is click on the link in my description and make your mix of the ingredients you like on your food.
After that, they'll ask you for your name and your cell phone number and then they will text you the coupon!

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a normal promotion does not resolve the central concern: the viewer is sent through an external link and asked for identifying contact information before receiving the promised coupon. The cited description does not establish who operates that destination or how the information is used. A stated purchase condition also means the benefit is not genuinely free in the ordinary sense.

citations.quote: click on the link in my description
they'll ask you for your name and your cell phone number
CHIPOTLE BOGO: https://savorwavs.com

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The action flow is consistent with obtaining a coupon, not evidence of a scam. The offer is explicitly described as buy-one-get-one food, and the video states that the coupon is texted after the viewer completes the process. Those facts show a qualifying purchase and delivery mechanism, but they do not show impersonation, theft, or a false reward.

citations.quote: They are offering a free burrito when you buy one
then they will text you the coupon!

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an unusually attractive food reward, an external link, collection of a name and cell phone number, and a stated expiration date and one-per-number limit. The video gives viewers a concrete reason to act quickly while directing them away from the video itself for the claim process. It does not establish the external destination's affiliation with Chipotle or explain why the requested information is necessary. That combination makes the offer materially risky rather than a sufficiently verified ordinary coupon.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the stated terms as reassurance, but an expiration date and per-number limit also create pressure and facilitate tracking. The external URL is presented as the route to the offer, yet nothing supplied verifies its affiliation or explains the data request. Attractive food imagery and a recognizable brand reference cannot authenticate the claim process.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are ordinary coupon limitations, not evidence of deception. The video describes a single-use limit and an expiration date, while clearly identifying the reward as a buy-one-get-one food offer. The absence of supplied verification about the destination may justify caution, but it does not establish that the offer is fraudulent.

opening.argument: Although presented as helpful savings advice, the video's practical function is to promote participation in a specific claim funnel. It names a branded buy-one-get-one offer, directs viewers to a description link, instructs them to configure their food, and tells them to submit personal contact details to obtain the coupon. The surrounding description reinforces this promotional role by placing the Chipotle BOGO link among numerous coupon and referral links. The educational framing therefore does not change the fact that viewers are being steered toward an external offer.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the offer's food subject while overlooking how the video drives viewers into an external process. Its title and explanation present the deal attractively, but the actual instruction is to click a supplied link and surrender contact information for the promised coupon. Describing the content as a promotion does not make that solicitation trustworthy.

Steering viewers to a deal is expected for coupon content. Nothing cited shows that the promotion is fabricated or that the requested contact information is misused.
